must_survive_findings: Per-pool demand decouples: vision (image) demand is nearly independent of the request rate a conventional autoscaler watches (R^2=0.12 vs 0.65 for decode; Jaccard 0.02 on top-percentile minutes), so no single signal can size every pool.

The signal most dangerous to reactive scaling is the most forecastable: the image signal is both the burstiest (CV^2 3.83 vs 0.32) and the most persistent (Hurst approx 0.93), and pretrained time-series foundation models forecast it zero-shot at provisioning horizons, beating classical baselines in all 20 (signal x resolution) cells.

In a silicon-calibrated two-pool simulation the pools' saturation knees sit an order of magnitude apart, and the encoder pool violates its tail SLO invisibly at the trace's own rate (p99 5.0s at 29% mean utilization) where rate/utilization monitors see a healthy pool.

Closing the loop, per-pool provisioning (forecast for vision, tail-aware conversion for language) holds the tail SLA through burst onsets that defeat an identically-informed reactive controller, at 0.62x the deployable static encoder fleet's GPU-time; anticipatory headroom (not signal choice) is the operative advantage and mean-based conversion is the language-pool's specific defect.

Methodological anchor that must survive: the encoder cost model was collected on real silicon (RTX 5090), validated physically (~3% on attention, within 12.8% against vLLM's own vision tower across N<=64) and upstreamed to AIC; the closed loop was replayed against the live Dynamo control plane.

tex/trace-eda.tex.role: The empirical-motivation chapter: characterizes the Azure multimodal trace to establish the workload facts (vision decoupled from request rate, bursty, forecastable) that justify a separate vision pool and predictive scaling — the premise the rest of the thesis builds on.

must_survive_findings: Vision work is decoupled from request rate: a constant-fraction model explains only R2=0.123 of image rate (vs 0.654 for decode), and the two pools' extreme-load minutes are essentially disjoint (Jaccard 0.02, 5 shared minutes) - provisioning vision from the request signal misses exactly the moments that matter.

The vision/image signal is simultaneously the burstiest AND the most persistent of the four demand signals (CV2 3.83 vs 0.32; 69-min vs 9-min autocorrelation memory; H~0.93) - burstiness and forecastable structure concentrate in the same vision-borne signal, which is the feasibility premise for predictive scaling.

Burstiness is scale-free: the arrival process is non-Poisson at every scale (Fano factor 1.8 at 1s -> 938 at 1h) and minute-resolution monitoring recovers under 4% of the true instantaneous image peak (vs 37% for requests) - no aggregation window smooths the vision surges away.

The trace contains essentially one burst type: frames-class floods (k>10 grids) supplying 93-96% of every top episode's image volume, ramping baseline-to-peak in a median 6 minutes; bursts compound on the prefill stage (2.69x prefill length) while decode stays nearly burst-neutral.

Framing structural facts: 50/50 text/multimodal split is by construction, images arrive as k^2 tile/frame batches (not independent images), and ContextTokens embeds the traced model's vision tokens non-additively - so the converter drives encoder work from NumImages separately.

tex/predictors.tex.role: Validates the thesis's central feasibility premise — that demand signals (esp. vision image-rate) are forecastable at provisioning horizons — by benchmarking 3 zero-shot TS foundation models vs 3 classical baselines and Dynamo's shipped predictors, producing the forecast signal the closed-loop chapters consume.
tex/predictors.tex.action: Tightest of the results chapters — offload per-config WAPE dumps (shipped-predictor 4-way numbers, quantile nested counts, coverage parentheticals) to DB, keeping one representative gap + the load-bearing p90=0.88-0.90. Consolidate the ~7 'the closed loop settles it' forward-references to 1-2. Say the no-skill-floor and common-span caveats once each.
must_survive_findings: Zero-shot foundation models beat every classical baseline in all 20 (resolution, signal) cells with no tuning: a modest 2-9% relative edge at provisioning cadence (1-min bins) widening to ~one-third on the image signal at 1-second bins — but 1s is the WAPE~100% no-skill floor, so the operative claim is 'usable at minutes, nothing forecasts single sub-minute bins.'

Horizon degradation is mild: foundation-model WAPE grows only a few points from h=1 to h=12, so the Chapter-EDA persistence translates into 12 minutes of usable lead time that covers the median vision burst onset.

Inter-model choice is noise-level (a three-way tie, several column wins decided by <=0.1 WAPE with no significance); and Dynamo's shipped predictors (ARIMA/Kalman/Prophet/constant) never reach the foundation-model level while foundation models don't dramatically beat them either — making the closed-loop predictor-choice result mechanical.

Cross-signal covariates are nearly irrelevant at provisioning cadence (the forecasting-side echo of pool decoupling, R^2=0.12 req->img), helping only in the sub-15s shot-noise regime; the stronger additive context-reconstruction variant fails because the image forecast is the worst component exactly at the burst onsets where the structural bet needed it.

The p90 upper band edge is empirically calibrated at 1-minute cadence (coverage 0.88-0.90 across models/signals), making upper-quantile headroom a sound provisioning input; but no fixed quantile improves on a median-point model's point path (band is headroom, not point correction), and the lower edge/band-width is distorted by zero-ties.

tex/twopool.tex.role: Composes the three prior ingredients (workload, forecasts, encoder cost model) into the running two-pool serving simulation and establishes the platform's three load-bearing results: timing fidelity, an exact encoder batching law + handoff bound, and the order-of-magnitude saturation-knee separation that motivates the rest of the thesis.

must_survive_findings: Calibrated per-request timing (AIC h100) exposes language-pool latency tails the mocker's default polynomial flattens (TTFT p99 1.24x, max TTFT/ITL ~2x); burst failure is visible ONLY under calibrated timing, so it must back every headline run.

The encoder cost model admits an exact batching law: a forward is priced by its total image count regardless of how images factor into (batch, images-per-request), grounding a greedy-FIFO chunk-parallel dispatch policy and an analytic handoff bound.

The central decoupling result, now a property of the simulated system: on steady traffic the two pools' saturation knees sit an order of magnitude apart (vision uncrossed at 32x the trace rate, language knee at s=2 calibrated), so sizing both off one signal overprovisions the encoder fleet >10x.

Inside the largest burst both pools violate the SLA at the naive 2x2 topology in structurally different ways: a REMOVABLE language-pool TP1 prefill floor (TP2 passes the same window) versus episodic vision-pool FIFO head-of-line queueing (p99 delay 5.0s at 29% mean utilization) that is invisible to rate- and utilization-based monitoring and yields only to capacity.
Secondary but load-bearing: under the dual-bound SLA the steady-window language pool is decode-bound (ITL), not TTFT-bound, so per-user token throughput sets its capacity envelope.

must_survive_findings: Encoder pool: the p90-forecast policy meets the tail SLA in all 60 issue-time cells (every window x model x lead, both readiness models), lead-invariant from 15 to 165 s, while the identically-informed reactive controller loses burst3 at every lead — and the mechanism is the calibrated p90 band's graduated standing headroom, NOT clean onset detection (the forecast lags the fastest onset). Week-scale economics: the p90 schedule meets the SLA in aggregate AND per-episode at 0.62x the deployable static encoder fleet (0.59-0.62x across readiness models); rho is a cost knob (0.48-0.89x frontier, only rho=25 drops cells). must_survive_findings: RQ1: the request-rate signal a conventional autoscaler watches does not carry the vision pool's demand — the pools' demands decouple and saturate an order of magnitude apart, so missizing requires a fleet-shape change (TP + worker count) no replica scaler can perform.

RQ2: three pretrained time-series foundation models forecast the vision signal zero-shot, beating every classical baseline across all cells at provisioning horizons, with an empirically calibrated p90 band.
RQ3: the encoder cost model was collected and validated on real silicon to within 12.8% of vLLM's own vision tower (the earlier 1.4-1.6x gap was HuggingFace execution overhead, not model error).

RQ4: the p90-forecast schedule holds the tail SLA at every cold-start lead — including the fast onset that defeats an identically-informed reactive controller — at ~0.62x the static encoder fleet's GPU-time; the load-bearing mechanism is the calibrated band SHAPE, not forecast accuracy, and the language pool needs a tail-aware capacity conversion.

The scope caveats that must survive: one seven-day trace with an offered-work upper bound on decode; the inter-pool handoff is an analytic single-stream bound (the 588ms floor and cost ratio assume embedding-only handoff or >=100Gbps); the vision control loop is simulated against measured silicon, not yet a live serving loop.
